title: Identifying a Vector Autoregression from Covariances of Temporally Aggregated Flow Sums
banked_reason: The field-tier assumption-removal claim remains priority-borderline until theorem-level comparisons are obtained for Telser (1967), Lütkepohl (1987, Chapter 8), Gómez–Aparicio-Pérez (2009), Hansen–Sargent (1983), and Casals–Jerez–Sotoca (2009); the sound kernel therefore achieves subfield tier.
gap_reasons: The field-tier assumption-removal claim remains priority-borderline until theorem-level comparisons are obtained for Telser (1967), Lütkepohl (1987, Chapter 8), Gómez–Aparicio-Pérez (2009), Hansen–Sargent (1983), and Casals–Jerez–Sotoca (2009), whose accessible material does not establish whether any proves this exact dense three-covariance all-flow inverse.
proof_attempt_summary: Three D-0.5 proposal iterations preserved a sound constructive matrix-recovery kernel while first correcting the bibliography and then reframing the contribution as an exact assumption-removal result relative to Gong et al. (2017). The distinct Gong-relative reframe removed broad priority claims and isolated Anderson et al. as non-nested, but the reviewer still required theorem-level access to five classical flow/disaggregation sources for field novelty. The result is therefore banked at subfield tier before D0 formal derivation; a future re-raise should reuse the final proto core and supply those primary theorem texts rather than repeat the proposal revisions.
tldr: Can three population covariance matrices of known aligned all-coordinate \(k\)-period sums globally determine a stable nonsingular labeled VAR(1)? The proposal seeks a theorem-level assumption removal relative to Gong et al. for the same flow operator: replace non-Gaussian independent-component separation and its sign-resolution conditions by temporal whiteness and \(D\succ0\), derive \(B=A^k\), solve the induced Riccati equation through one positive matrix square root, and constructively recover dense labeled \(A,P,D\) in every finite dimension. Anderson et al.'s fast-channel theorem is non-nested, and structural autonomy and causal shock semantics remain separate maintained assumptions.
gap: For the same aligned uniform all-coordinate flow operator, Gong et al. identify \(A^k\) from delayed covariances and recover \(A\) through non-Gaussian independent-component structure plus sign-resolution conditions. It remains to establish whether second-order temporal whiteness and \(D\succ0\) alone select the dense labeled fine-time transition and recover \(P,D\) from exactly \(\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2\). Anderson et al.'s second-order theorem retains a fast channel and is therefore non-nested; scalar-flow and stock-sampling results address different parameter spaces or operators.
fill: Prove a strict theorem-level strengthening of Gong et al. on the finite-second-moment overlap: establish the noncommutative covariance identities and inverse domains; show that \(HK^{-1}H-H=JK^{-1}J^{\mathsf T}\) has exactly one positive solution; recover \(A,P,D\) explicitly without non-Gaussianity or contemporaneous independence; derive local smoothness; and state causal consequences only under separate autonomous structural assumptions.
